findings.summary: When `entry` is present but not an array of tables, the error reports `entry 0` even though no entry was indexed.
findings.evidence: In parse_entries, `as_array_of_tables().ok_or(LedgerError::NotATable { index: 0 })` reports index 0 for a top-level type error. A top-level variant without an index would be clearer.

findings.summary: The requirement says Athena is critiqued 'to the same standard'; check_standard only checks that an Athena entry exists.
findings.evidence: check_standard only checks `entries.iter().any(|e| e.subject == ATHENA)`. This limit is disclosed in the module doc, the spec mechanism, CHANGELOG, the map row (Partial), and ledger entry L-001, and the accepted reading allows it. The measure stays `status: not shown`.

summary: This retry does what the request asked and fixes the earlier failure. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --test critique_ledger` and all 9 tests passed. They cover the real ledger and the spec entry, plus negative cases for a duplicate id, an unknown kind, an unknown status, an unknown key, blank text, a missing Athena entry, a missing kind, and an empty or malformed ledger. The stale-view test that failed last time, `cargo test -p athena-cli --lib strategy_view_table_matches_the_map`, now passes. Its edited counts match what `athena strategy` prints (G6 partial 8 / not covered 15; total partial 69 / not covered 39). For fmt, clippy and the full test suite I relied on Athena's recorded passes for this same commit (CI run 43390509283) rather than rerunning them. All 9 changed files are on the expected deliverables list. docs/decisions.md and records/ are untouched. Two small findings remain. The Athena check only confirms an Athena entry exists, which is weaker than "the same standard"; this is disclosed in several places and the accepted reading allows it (minor). And an error message reports "entry 0" for a whole-file type error (nit).
